text:
sara_dev: Quick ask — trying to pin concurrency targets for Dedicated pools if we onboarded the new 65B-q4 model. Need numbers for US/EU/APAC to feed planning.

mike_platform: ran a small bench this morning (dev cluster). Results below, rough but directional.
```
h100-us-west: concurrency 8 -> p50 85ms, p95 210ms, qps ~48
a100-eu-west: concurrency 6 -> p50 140ms, p95 340ms, qps ~28
h100-ap-southeast: concurrency 7 -> p50 110ms, p95 290ms, qps ~34
``` 
note: batch=1, seq_len=1024, kv-cache warmed for repeated prefixes.

ajay_ml: thanks — what's the kernel mix? q4f16 on h100 used fused attention kernels? any tiling fallback on a100?

mike_platform: h100 run used cu-attn-fused + int8 paths for gpt-block; a100 run fell back to tiled matmul on some layers (we saw kernel mismatch on layer 24+), which explains the p95 gap.

jen_ops: perf numbers look fine. For capacity planning we need concurrency target per GPU and autoscale headroom. What's your recommended concurrency to keep p95 under 300ms in each region?

ajay_ml: rough rule: pick concurrency that keeps p95 < 2.5x p50. From the runs:
- h100-us-west: concurrency 8 is good (p95 210ms)
- a100-eu-west: drop to concurrency 5 to bring p95 ~260-280ms
- h100-ap-southeast: concurrency 7 seems OK but reserve headroom

mike_platform: can confirm. Also add 25-30% autoscale headroom for bursts + cache cold-starts. If you want predictable SLA, aim for conservative packing (70% of theoretical qps).

ops-bot: Autoscale snapshot (last 7d typical) — us-west peak concurrent sessions: 420, eu-west peak: 310, ap-southeast peak: 180. Avg CPU/infra headroom at peak: ~28%.

sara_dev: If we pick concurrency targets: us-west 8, eu-west 5, ap-southeast 6 — how many GPUs to reserve for a 99th percentile day with 30% headroom? Rough calc?

mike_platform: quick calc: use peak concurrent sessions / (concurrency * 0.7 packing) rounded up.
- us-west: 420 / (8 * 0.7) = 75 -> 75 GPUs
- eu-west: 310 / (5 * 0.7) = 89 -> 89 GPUs
- ap-southeast: 180 / (6 * 0.7) = 43 -> 43 GPUs

ajay_ml: those eu numbers look high because a100 concurrency is lower. We could instead offer a smaller pool with auto-burst to h100 in another region as fallback for enterprise customers.

jen_ops: action: create a canary pool of 10 h100 in eu for overflow routing, and set autoscale threshold to trigger once queued requests > 250 for 30s. Also create a job to re-run kernel sweep on a100 to try improved kernel selection.

sara_dev: sounds good. Next steps: mike to run an extended benchmark (24h) with mixed seq lengths and some cold-cache startups; ajay to attempt kernel tuning sweep on a100; jen to draft capacity ask numbers for finance.

mike_platform: will kick off the 24h bench today. posting raw logs link in a sec: https://internal.redwood/bench/4105551234

ajay_ml: I'll start kernel sweep tomorrow morning and ping if I find a tiling patch that reduces p95.

jen_ops: drafting the capacity ask now — will include the numbers above and note the fallback strategy.

sara_dev: perfect. thanks all :thumbsup:
